scope.description: Observe what LeadershipTransferToServer reports against which server actually takes leadership when the requested target is a non-voter, with the same call naming a voter as the only difference. Each case emits an assurance_transfer_target setup event describing the leader, the chosen target, its suffrage in the leader's latest configuration and the voter set, then an assurance_transfer_result event with the returned result, the target's and old leader's states, the leader set and terms after the call, and the time until any leader is observed.
assumptions: Three voters plus one non-voter is a supported configuration; the non-voter is joined through the leader's own AddNonvoter call.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate; protocol version is the default (>= 3), so LeadershipTransferToServer is supported.
A voter target is a legal and expected use, so the voter case is the control that the probe can observe a real transfer rather than a probe that never succeeds.
excluded: Bounding the length of any leaderless interval: leadership state is sampled at the end of the 1500ms observation window, so this probe does not measure an interval.

basis.prefix: Each case builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts. Three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster from a configuration naming them as Voter; the fourth node is started without a configuration and joined through the elected leader's own AddNonvoter(id, address, 0, 5s) call, waiting until the leader's latest configuration reports it. The target is then chosen by configuration role, never by a measured result: in the control case the first voter that is not the leader, in the probe case the joined non-voter; its suffrage is read back from the leader's latest configuration and reported in the setup event. The case calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(target.id, target.addr), waits up to 5s for the returned result, then waits up to 1500ms for the requested target to be observed as Leader and separately for any node to be Leader, and finally records the leader set, the maximum term across all four nodes and whether that term rose above the leader's term before the call. Both cases share the harness TestAssuranceLeadershipTransferTarget and are emitted under distinct case names.

comparisons.description: Non-voter target: what the call reported. Holds means the predicted success report was observed, which supports the defect account rather than contradicting it.
Non-voter target: the requested server never became leader within the observation window.
Voter target control: the same call does transfer leadership, so the non-voter outcome is not a probe that never transfers.
Voter target control: the reported result for a transfer that does complete.
